sentences: `tools/lane_masks.py` tracks per-lane mask bits through scalar registers, vector operations and saved EXEC spills.

Whole-mask counts, first-set-lane queries, the leading-bit scans `s_flbit_i32_b32` / `s_flbit_i32` of `vcc_lo`/`exec_lo` (and `_hi`) and equality use subgroup operations (`tests/semantic/test_salu_flbit_lane_mask.py`; until then the flbit scans saw this lane's 0 / ~0).
Whole-mask counts, first-set-lane queries and equality use subgroup operations.
`cs_wavemask` checks all 64 lanes with a partially active EXEC mask.

A physical 32-lane subgroup cannot directly exchange mask bits with the other half of a wave64, so `cs_wavemask` and the `cs_wave64_ballot` / `cs_wm_*` tests are exact only on 64-wide subgroups (AMD): on an RTX 4090 (subgroup 32) `s_bcnt1_i32_b64` of lanes 16–47 counts 16, one half (#101).
`check.py` skips them where the GPU has no 64-wide compute subgroup.

A mask copied into a VGPR with `v_mov_b32` goes through the normal EXEC-gated store, so inactive lanes keep the old VGPR (SHADER-21 part 2, #210); per-lane mask computations still store in all lanes, because whole-wave readers (`wave_mask`, `v_readfirstlane`) read every lane's bit.
